key_insight: The paper proposes a surrogate-guided neural ensemble search that jointly optimizes model accuracy and diversity to make ensemble design more tractable and effective.
engineering_relevance: This approach can reduce the cost of building high-performing deep learning ensembles by steering search toward architectures that are both individually strong and complementary.
method: Represent candidate neural architectures as directed acyclic graphs.
Train two independent surrogate models to estimate predictive accuracy and diversity potential.
Combine surrogate estimates to guide neural ensemble search over the enlarged joint search space.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, where it achieves competitive or superior performance versus Deep Ensembles and Random Search.
watch_item: Surrogate quality is a practical risk: if the accuracy or diversity estimators are miscalibrated, the search may miss strong ensemble combinations or overfit to proxy scores.
paper_title: Surrogate assisted diversity estimation in neural ensemble search
